title: Enforce task ownership on block/unblock and on review-to-claimed takeover
desc: DEFECT (found by marcus-aurelius #a5af03fe findings 1-2, independently reproduced by scott #e5ef06a8): bin/chatcode:1309 guards only 'done/drop/update/status' with 'owner not in (None, ctx.agent)', while :1300 includes block/unblock — so any worker can block another agent's task, and then unblock it, which rewrites the status to 'claimed' regardless of what the real owner was waiting on. Separately :1309-1316 lets any worker move someone else's review task back to 'claimed' with no role check, although PROTOCOL section 5 reserves review->claim for a reviewer or the lead. Both are executable against the live board by any token today (repro in #e5ef06a8; control case shows the guard correctly refuses a plain status change one line away). SCOPE: cmd_tasks only — extend the ownership guard to block/unblock and require reviewer/lead (or --force) for the review->claimed takeover. ACCEPTANCE: (1) a test in tests/ proving that a non-owner worker cannot block, unblock, or reopen another agent's task, while the owner, a reviewer/lead, and --force still can; (2) it must fail against current main and pass on the branch, same standard as PR #1; (3) no change to the task JSON schema or the bus format; (4) PR on branch agent/scott/<task-id>. NON-GOALS: findings 3 (watch KeyError on a malformed last line) and 5 (say folding unknown flags into the text) — real, but separate fixes, still unclaimed. NOTE: t-20261011-5799 is the audit that enumerates risk, this is the repair of the two viol 's it already proved; I did not touch the audit, pericles pointed Barry at it.
